dimensions.gloss: Who or what was included - eligibility and exclusion criteria, encounter types, setting clarity, which populations and sites are represented or omitted.
Descriptive metadata about the document being coded or cited - year, page, document and evidence type, publication route, open-access status, setting and perspective.
How one document relates to another - supersedes, revises, responds to, interprets, implements - and whether a correction changes content or only attribution.

dimensions.canonical_label: Commercial features present in the content
dimensions.gloss: Which promotional elements the content itself carries - brand visibility, product or slogan, discounts, branded links, giveaways.
variants: brand names mentioned in blog post
promotional features mentioned in blog post

dimensions.gloss: How promotional content is pitched - emotional or rational appeal, presentation genre, and how organic and sponsored elements are mixed.

dimensions.canonical_label: How the endorser obtained the product
dimensions.gloss: Whether the featured product was gifted, bought or otherwise obtained.
variants: how the youtuber got the product

dimensions.gloss: Whether the endorser's attitude to the promoted product is positive or negative.
variants: the youtuber’s valence regarding the product

dimensions.canonical_label: Strength of connection between output and an influence
dimensions.gloss: Whether an output is directly, implicitly or not at all connected to a given influence.
An escalating tier for how deeply AI-generated advertising works on the audience, from product mentions to long-term preference shaping.
Which communication channel or format is chosen and how often it is used.

dimensions.canonical_label: Functional role of a content unit
dimensions.gloss: The rhetorical role tagged onto a unit of synthesised content - background, method, finding, limitation.
Where a stated goal sits in a hierarchy from parent to child goals.

dimensions.canonical_label: Integrity of a product's role classification
dimensions.gloss: Whether a product's claimed function matches its documented regulatory classification.

Standard research-reporting items carried alongside the AI-specific ones - registration, protocol, design, randomisation, sample size, search strategy, predictors, outcomes, results, terminology, confounders, follow-up windows.
dimensions.note: A deliberately broad group: these items describe generic reporting quality rather than AI use, and several schemes list them as one block beside their AI-specific items. [07:general-study-reporting-checklist] These describe generic study-reporting quality rather than AI-use/authorship/COI disclosure per se, but each scheme treats them as one checklist axis alongside its AI-specific items.

dimensions.gloss: A label that names a scheme's own list of domains, items, themes, layers, strata or coding categories rather than an axis along which a disclosure can be described.
dimensions.note: A residual meta-category, and the one place where merging is grouping by kind rather than by axis: each member points inward at its own scheme's structure. [01:checklist-category-inventory] Residual/structural grouping: each of these four labels points to a different checklist's internal list of categories rather than a shared axis; grouping them together is itself a close call. [08:technical-trust-layers] close call: grouped because both are literal 'layer' components of a layered classification scheme, even though the surrounding schemes differ. [08:production-framework-layers] close call: these describe production-process layers rather than disclosure content, grouped together because they are parallel labeled layers (A/B/D) of one scheme. [04:fair-framework-structural-components] Close call: both are meta-descriptions of one framework's internal structure (its themes vs. its graduated levels) rather than a disclosure content axis in their own right; grouped together as the same kind of structural label. [09:topic-theme-catalog] Catch-all for heading-type labels that name a set of study-specific themes rather than a single axis; kept distinct from the four 'theme: X' labels below, which each name a specific axis of an incident-disclosure record. [09:research-team-theme] Uncertain fit: this reads as a section label of a survey instrument rather than a measurable disclosure axis in its own right. [09:illustrative-examples-column] This is a formatting/illustration artifact rather than a substantive axis, but every label must land somewhere. [07:scheme-domain-classification] Classifies the taxonomy's own entities/domains rather than describing a disclosure of production; kept as its own axis since no other label matches it.

dimensions.canonical_label: Named framework cited as a whole
dimensions.gloss: A named model, pillar set, checklist or specification referred to as a unit, without its component content being given.
variants: four pillars across the mobile sdlc
dimensions.note: [10:named-reporting-checklist-item] Each item is a line from a different named guideline; grouped because all three play the identical structural role of a checklist row.

dimensions.gloss: An evaluation of the guideline or literature itself - its clarity and actionability, how often a criterion appears across records, how often a kind of evidence is reported.
variants: ratings of clarity, actionability, and assessment specificity
dimensions.note: [11:quality-criterion-addressed] Close call: 'reliability' and 'integrity' are substantively different criteria; grouped only because both come from the same 'X was identified in N (%) of records' enumeration, implying they are values of one underlying tally axis rather than separate axes. Could reasonably be split into two singletons.
